presentation_outline: 1. Physics Question & Motivation: How motion spreads through an initially stationary fluid, and why we need both dynamic viscosity (mu) and kinematic viscosity (nu).
2. Physical Intuition Before PDEs: How unequal horizontal shear forces on a thin fluid layer cause acceleration, and why steady linear flow has zero net acceleration despite nonzero velocity.
3. Predict & Observe Walkthrough: Live demonstration of the four guided experiments (doubling rho, doubling mu, doubling both rho and mu, and doubling gap H).
4. Free Exploration & Numerical Design: How explicit FTCS stability (Fo <= 0.5), grid resolution, and the t = 0 wall-stress singularity are handled.
5. AI Critique Decisions: Why specific suggestions were accepted (e.g., bounded inputs, solver contract) or rejected (e.g., omitting shear-stress readouts/graphs to avoid clutter).
6. Two-Model Comparison (Astra vs. Gemini): Attempt 1 findings, the single consolidated correction round, Attempt 2 results, and final selection criteria.
7. Student Takeaways & Future Questions: Lessons learned about transport phenomena pedagogy and structured evaluation of AI-generated scientific software.
